application_guidance.input_pattern: Compare dimension and absolute accuracy for deterministic bounded exact-value smooth convex minimization.
read_original_when: Adapting to noisy values, randomization, unbounded queries, higher regularity or fixed condition number.
sensitive_conditions: Absolute, not relative, accuracy; global beta-smoothness and inner minimizer promise.
Exact-real value evaluations allow arbitrarily small h without a bit-cost charge.
Only the moderate-accuracy interval is matched.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic uniform worst-instance upper guarantee and deterministic minimax lower bound, with separate parameter ranges.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: c,C,c_epsilon,d0 universal, independent of d,R,beta,epsilon; explicit upper constant 6.
complexity_scope.oracle: At time t a deterministic Borel map Q_t:(X x R)^(t-1)->X chooses x_t from the exact history (x_i,f(x_i)); a Borel Q_out:(X x R)^T->X returns any feasible point, which need not have been queried. The unknown objective is fixed. Only exact scalar f(x) is returned; arbitrary exact-real internal computation is free. Repeated oracle calls count; reuse of an already stored value makes no new call.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Lower covers every feasible xhat in X including unqueried points. Upper witness outputs x_N in C. Absolute gap f(xhat)-min f, not relative error.
complexity_scope.regime: Upper, lower and matching regimes as stated separately; high-accuracy lower bound saturates.
complexity_scope.resource: Number of exact scalar function-value calls; repeated calls charged, cache reuse free; internal exact-real computations uncharged.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Upper witness: coordinate forward differences inside an error-robust accelerated projected method. Lower coverage: all feasible deterministic adaptive Borel exact-value policies.

content.intended_use: Compare dimension and absolute accuracy for deterministic bounded exact-value smooth convex minimization.

proofs.locator: Lemmas 4.1–4.3, equations (4.3)–(4.19); proof of Theorem 3.3; proofs of Theorem 3.5 and Corollaries 3.6–3.7
map: On C, a gradient error ||g-grad f(y)||<=delta_g gives lower model error delta_l=R delta_g and upper model error delta_u=delta_g^2/(2beta) with bar_beta=2beta (Lemma 4.2, convexity, smoothness and Young).

Section 4.2 initializes x0=z0=0,A0=0 and psi0(x)=||x||^2/2. At step k choose alpha>0 with A_new=A_k+alpha=bar_beta alpha^2; y=(A_k x_k+alpha z_k)/A_new; add alpha[f(y)+<g,x-y>] to psi; z_new=argmin_C psi_new=Pi_C(-sum_i alpha_i g_i); x_new=(A_k x_k+alpha z_new)/A_new. Convex combinations keep all base points in C.

Lemma 4.3 proves psi_k^*>=A_k f(x_k)-E_k with E_new=E_k+A_k delta_l+A_new delta_u. Evaluating psi_N at x^* yields f(x_N)-f^*<=||x^*||^2/(2 A_N)+(N+1)delta_l+N delta_u, A_N>=N^2/(4bar_beta). This is a source-linked estimate-sequence proof, not an extra local theorem.

Choose N=ceil(2sqrt(Q)), delta_g=epsilon/[8R(N+1)], h=2delta_g/(beta sqrt(d))<=R/2. The linked finite-difference lemma uses d+1 values per step and gives this gradient error. With ||x^*||<=R/2 the three errors are <=epsilon/4, epsilon/8, epsilon/128, hence gap<epsilon. Calls (d+1)N<=6d sqrt(Q).

Import the linked integer lower theorem. In Section 12 let M=min{sqrt(Q),(d/log(ed))^(1/3)}, choose universal a<=1/4, a^3<=c0, a^2<=2^(-18), c_epsilon=a^2/4; enlarge d0 so M>=2/a and a(d/log(ed))^(1/3)<=d/4. Then m=floor(a M) satisfies (a/2)M<=m<=a M and m^3 log(ed)<=c0 d. The integer error bound >=2^(-17)beta R^2/m^2>=2epsilon, so T<dm/8 fails and N_epsilon>=dm/8>=(a/16)d M.
The branch threshold follows by comparing sqrt(Q) and (d/log(ed))^(1/3); combining the sqrt lower branch with the upper theorem proves Corollary 3.6 in exactly the stated accuracy interval.
proofs.omitted_details: Long source-linked proof map; no full independent reproof of the accelerated method or integer theorem. Source sometimes calls numbered Lemmas/Corollaries/Propositions Theorem in cross-references; locators here use the actual numbered objects.
proofs.reading_coverage: Native images and direct PDF Section 4, plus direct PDF Section 12 and the actual statements pp.6–8. No whole-paper reading asserted.

assumptions: Use precisely this global objective class and feasible exact-value information model.
Upper and lower statements have separate dimension and accuracy domains; the matched rate is only their stated intersection.
statement.conclusion: Upper: N_epsilon<=(d+1)ceil(2sqrt(Q))<=6d sqrt(Q); all queries in X, output in C. Lower: N_epsilon>=c d min{sqrt(Q),(d/log(ed))^(1/3)}. Therefore universal c,C>0 give c d sqrt(Q)<=N_epsilon<=C d sqrt(Q) throughout the matching window. Subject to the lower theorem thresholds, Q<=(d/log(ed))^(2/3) selects the sqrt(Q) lower branch, whereas Q>=(d/log(ed))^(2/3) gives only c d^(4/3)/log(ed)^(1/3). No matching high-accuracy rate is asserted.
statement.objects_and_definitions: X=B_2^d(R), C=B_2^d(R/2). F_beta(d,R) consists of convex C^1 functions f:R^d->R with globally beta-Lipschitz gradient in Euclidean norm and a unique global minimizer x_f^* in C; f^*=min_R^d f. At time t a deterministic Borel map Q_t:(X x R)^(t-1)->X chooses x_t from the exact history (x_i,f(x_i)); a Borel Q_out:(X x R)^T->X returns any feasible point, which need not have been queried. The unknown objective is fixed. Only exact scalar f(x) is returned; arbitrary exact-real internal computation is free. Repeated oracle calls count; reuse of an already stored value makes no new call. N_epsilon is the infimum of integer T>=0 for which a deterministic T-call policy satisfies sup_{f in F_beta}(f(xhat_f)-f^*)<=epsilon, with inf empty=+infinity. Q=beta R^2/epsilon and log is natural.
statement.parameter_domains: Upper: d in N, R,beta>0, 0<epsilon<=beta R^2. Lower: d>=d0, 0<epsilon<=c_epsilon beta R^2. Constants may be decreased/increased so 0<c_epsilon<=1. Matching window: beta R^2(log(ed)/d)^(2/3)<=epsilon<=c_epsilon beta R^2.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: Upper: for every d>=1,R,beta>0,0<epsilon<=beta R^2 there exists a deterministic feasible algorithm working uniformly over F_beta. Lower: universal c,c_epsilon>0,d0 exist such that for every d>=d0,R,beta>0,0<epsilon<=c_epsilon beta R^2 all covered deterministic policies obey the minimax lower bound. No random success parameter.

checked_locators: Definitions 3.1–3.2, Theorems 3.3–3.5 and Corollaries 3.6–3.7, pp.6–8; Sections 4 and 12
use_restrictions: The lower bound covers deterministic adaptive Borel policies with bounded queries and output; it is not a randomized, unrestricted-query, C^2/C^infinity or fixed-condition-number lower bound.
High-accuracy matching and arithmetic/bit complexity are not established. Long proofs remain source-linked.
